title: Circuit breaker
short: Stop calling a failing service for a while so failure doesn't spread.
what: When a service you depend on is down, every call waits for a timeout, requests pile up, and your service falls over too. A circuit breaker counts failures; after too many it opens and fails calls at once. After a pause it lets one test call through, and closes again if that works.
analogy: The breaker in your house. A short circuit trips it so the wiring doesn't burn; you flip it back once the fault is fixed.

frames.say: A product page calls a Reviews service through a breaker. It starts Closed: every call goes through as normal.
Reviews gets overloaded. Calls time out after 2 s each, and the breaker counts failures in a row: 3 of 5 so far.
The 5th failure in a row trips the breaker to Open. Calls now fail at once instead of each hanging for 2 s.
While Open, the page loads without the reviews box. Reviews gets no calls from us, which gives it room to recover.
After 30 s the breaker moves to Half-open and lets one test call through, to see if Reviews is back.
The test call times out too, so it's straight back to Open for another 30 s. A sick service never gets a flood.
The next test call answers in 80 ms. The breaker closes, the count resets to 0, and the reviews come back.

when: A service you call is slow or down
Stop one failure from spreading to every service
Show a fallback instead of hanging
output:
t= 0s -> timeout 1 of 5
t= 2s -> timeout 2 of 5
t= 4s -> timeout 3 of 5
t= 6s -> timeout 4 of 5
t= 8s -> timeout, trips to OPEN
t= 9s -> OPEN: fail fast, 0 ms
t=40s -> test failed, OPEN again
t=75s -> ok, CLOSED again
cost: ~0 ms instead of a 2 s timeout
O(1): a counter and a time
watch: Have a fallback for the Open state (cached data, hide the box), not a blank error page.
Count only real failures like timeouts and 500s, not a 404 from bad input.
Pair it with timeouts. Without one, a hung call never counts as a failure.
interview: What happens when a service you depend on is slow?
